title: A Sales Type column you turn on stays on when you sign in again
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Scenario: You turn on the Sales Type column of Sales By Representative, then sign out and sign in again.
  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The Sales Type column of Sales By Representative is off for you.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open the column selector.
  2. Turn Sales Type on.
  3. Sign out.
  4. Sign in again.
  5. Open Reports > Sales By Representative.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the column selector opens, with Sales Type off.
  • Step 2: a Sales Type column shows right after Status, and before Location when the Location column shows; it holds words only (no money).
  • Step 3: you are signed out.
  • Step 4: you are signed in.
  • Step 5: the Sales Type column is still on.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R19: “An invoice row carries a "Sales Type" column, after Status and before Location (Status, Sales Type, Location), reading "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" or "Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R22: “A user who turns the Sales Type column on keeps it on for later visits.”
  • S5-R24: “The Sales Type column holds no money, so the report's existing rules for who may see money apply to the other columns unchanged.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 26: “26. (a) Status, Sales Type, Location.”
